equanimity

ee-kwuh-NIM-i-tee · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Equanimity is mental calm and a steady temper, especially in a difficult situation.

The chess champion studied the board with equanimity, unbothered by the ticking clock or the muttering crowd.

Worked Example

The veteran nurse delivered the difficult diagnosis with equanimity, her calm, steady voice helping the frightened family absorb the news.

Equanimity isn't coldness -- it's staying steady and composed on the inside even when a situation is upsetting.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

composure: Composure is self-control held together in one tense moment -- you keep your composure through the interview or the emergency. Equanimity runs deeper: an even temper that meets good fortune and bad with the same steadiness, not just one crisis.

serenity: Serenity is a peaceful, untroubled calm -- the mood of a still lake or a quiet evening, and it belongs to moments when nothing is wrong. Equanimity is calm that holds when something is wrong: an even temper kept through difficulty and good luck alike.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

agitation: a state of anxious excitement or nervousness

turmoil: a state of great disturbance or confusion

Where it sits · how complete the inner calm is — patience → equanimity → imperturbability

patience vs. equanimity: Patience is simply tolerating delay or difficulty without complaint, calmer but less complete than the deep composure of equanimity.

imperturbability vs. equanimity: Imperturbability is an even deeper, near-unshakable calm than ordinary equanimity, one that almost nothing can disturb.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — equ-

root — equ-: equal, even (Latin aequus)

root — anim-

root — anim-: mind, spirit (Latin animus)

suffix — -ity

suffix — -ity: state of, quality of (Latin/French)

Put it together

Put it together: Equanimity combines Latin aequus ('equal, even') with animus ('mind, spirit') plus -ity ('state of') -- literally 'the state of having an even mind,' or steady composure.

Word Choice

Equanimity specifically describes calm composure under stress or difficulty -- it's most powerful used to describe someone who stays steady in a moment that would upset most people.
